correctness.rationale: For every finite K>=2 and alpha_i>0, Dirichlet gamma moments differentiated with respect to the exponent yield the exact H-Q cross moment; algebra simplifies it to a strictly negative rational term plus a nonpositive weighted digamma covariance. The latter is nonnegative by pairwise monotonicity; positivity of every shape yields strictness. A second-order fixed-sum perturbation has coefficient proportional to 2a(Ka+1) trigamma(a+1)-1, and an integral representation proves this strictly increases through zero exactly once. Critical degeneracy and global extremality are explicitly excluded. A separate checker passes unsimplified mixed-moment, beta quadrature and curvature tests.

originality.rationale: The principal novel combination is the exact all-asymmetric strict entropy–collision covariance decomposition and the unique symmetric local-Hessian reversal at fixed total Dirichlet concentration. The ordinary mixed moment follows by differentiation of standard Dirichlet moments and is disclaimed as a standalone novelty. Closest papers respectively study compositional diversity estimation, power-sum priors, and marginal Gini–Simpson prior/posterior moments; the matched published-record results address distinct probability objects. Historical priority remains non-exhaustively checked.

value.rationale: Joint calibration of Shannon entropy and collision/Gini–Simpson diversity under Dirichlet priors is natural in ecological diversity and Bayesian multinomial modeling. The theorem settles universal direction of dependence for arbitrary asymmetric pseudo-counts and locates a genuinely different low-/high-concentration behavior of sensitivity to shape imbalance. The global sign decomposition and unique constrained-Hessian switch are structural; finite numerical root values merely illustrate them.
